cognitive.name: Shadesmar
cognitive.blurb: Roshar’s subastral, the best known. Where Roshar has land there is an ocean of glass beads, each the soul of an object; where it has seas there is dark, obsidian-like ground. Spren live here openly, in cities such as Celebrant and the honorspren fortress of Lasting Integrity, and trade in Stormlight. People show as candle-like flames.

parent.status: Second planet · Shardworld of Honor, Cultivation and Odium
parent.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart
parent.blurb: A world of stone and wind scoured by highstorms that roll in from the east every few days. One supercontinent, also called Roshar, holds nearly all its life. Plants pull into the rock when the storm comes, animals carry shells, and spheres left out in a storm fill with Stormlight. The Alethi princes fight an endless war on the Shattered Plains, while old stories speak of Desolations and of the Knights Radiant.
parent.short: The storm world of the Stormlight Archive.

5.status: Second planet · Shardworld of Honor, Cultivation and Odium · the Everstorm

8.blurb: A world of stone and wind scoured by highstorms from the east, and now by the Everstorm blowing the other way. The Knights Radiant have returned, the singers have woken, and Odium’s Fused are back from Braize. Dalinar Kholin tries to hold a coalition of nations together through the True Desolation.

12.status: Retribution’s world · cut off in slowed time
12.blurb: Dalinar challenged Odium to a contest of champions and, holding Honor’s power at the end, renounced it. Odium took Honor’s power into his own and became Retribution, killed the Stormfather, drew all Stormlight from the world and turned the highstorm into a planet-wide Everstorm. Time on Roshar has slowed, so about a decade there passes for decades elsewhere. Azir, Urithiru and the Shattered Plains resist his rule. Provisional account based on the Coppermind wiki; not independently checked against the book.

sites.name: The Valley
sites.desc: A hot, overgrown valley where the Nightwatcher grants boons and curses. Dalinar sought her here; Lift asked to stay young.

landmarks.name: The Nightwatcher’s valley
landmarks.desc: A warm, overgrown valley where people come to the Old Magic for a boon and a curse. Taravangian’s boon from her shapes everything he does.

sites.name: Azimir
sites.desc: Azir’s capital, with the Bronze Palace and the Grand Market dome over the Makabakam Oathgate. Lift steals food here; Azir is run by scribes and forms.

landmarks.name: The Bronze Palace
landmarks.desc: Seat of the Prime Aqasix. Lift breaks in to steal food, and the boy Gawx, whom she heals, is chosen as Prime.

landmarks.name: The Grand Market
landmarks.desc: An indoor market under a great bronze dome, built over the city’s Oathgate. The Azish fortify it once they learn what is underneath.

landmarks.name: The Makabakam Oathgate
landmarks.desc: The platform under the market dome, which Lift unlocks to open the way to Urithiru.

sites.name: Yeddaw
sites.desc: A Tashikki city made of Shardblade-cut trenches spiralling to the Grand Indicium, where Lift faces the Herald Nale in Edgedancer.

landmarks.name: The guarded entrance
landmarks.desc: A guarded entrance with a long line of people waiting to enter; Lift sneaks toward the front.

landmarks.name: The market
landmarks.desc: Lift watches the man she calls Darkness execute a girl here for stealing fruit.

landmarks.name: The Grand Indicium
landmarks.desc: A huge records building towering over the city. Lift talks her way in as an envoy from Azir to find who Darkness is hunting.

landmarks.name: The slots
landmarks.desc: The city’s deep cut channels, where farmers grow crops out of season.

codex.name: Lift
codex.desc: A young Reshi thief who breaks into palaces for the food, with a power she calls her awesomeness.
more: An Edgedancer, who stands up to the Herald Nale in Yeddaw.
